title: Urmila in the Ramcharitmanas: Wedding at Janakpur
description: Meet Urmila in Bal Kand, Doha 325 of the Ramcharitmanas, where King Janaka summons her with Mandavi and Shrutakirti during the wedding celebrations.
answer: Urmila is one of the three princesses whom King Janaka summons in bridal attire during the wedding celebrations in the Ramcharitmanas. Goswami Tulsidas names her alongside Mandavi and Shrutakirti in Bal Kand, Doha 325. Her appearance follows the marriage of Shri Ram and Mata Sita, as the wedding narrative turns to the other princesses.

sections.md:
The marriage of Shri Ram and Mata Sita has filled the assembly with joy. In Bal Kand, Doha 325, Goswami Tulsidas first shows them seated together on an exalted seat. King Dashrath rejoices at the sight, and the celebration extends throughout the universe. Against this background, Urmila enters the narrative.

At Sage Vashishtha's direction, King Janaka sends for Mandavi, Shrutakirti and Urmila, each dressed as a bride. The account thus moves from the marriage of Shri Ram and Mata Sita to the other princesses. Urmila's name belongs within this shared celebration at Janakpur.

sections.h2: What the passage tells us about Urmila
sections.md:
Goswami Tulsidas introduces Urmila by name and by her place among the princesses called to the wedding assembly. In Bal Kand, Doha 325, she appears with Mandavi and Shrutakirti. All three arrive in bridal attire at King Janaka's summons, following the direction of Sage Vashishtha.

We should attend carefully to whom each description belongs. The passage identifies Mandavi as the eldest daughter of Kushaketu, King Janaka's younger brother, and praises her qualities. Those particular details describe Mandavi. For Urmila, the account here gives a brief appearance within the wedding proceedings, without a separate description of her character.

A brief mention calls for attentive reading. In Bal Kand, Doha 325, Urmila has no recorded speech in the passage presented here. Goswami Tulsidas names her as the wedding proceedings continue, while the surrounding description dwells on the joy of Shri Ram and Mata Sita's marriage.

This gives us a clear place to begin understanding her appearance: the assembly, the summons and the bridal attire. It does not give an account of her later life or her experience during the exile. Read her introduction within the wedding narrative, allowing the details actually given to guide our understanding of the scene.

faq.q: Where is Urmila mentioned in the Ramcharitmanas?
faq.a: Urmila is named in Bal Kand, Doha 325, during the wedding celebrations at Janakpur. After describing Shri Ram and Mata Sita seated together, Goswami Tulsidas relates how King Janaka summons three other princesses at Sage Vashishtha's direction. They are Mandavi, Shrutakirti and Urmila, each dressed in bridal attire.

faq.q: Who appears with Urmila at the wedding?
faq.a: Mandavi and Shrutakirti are named alongside Urmila in Bal Kand, Doha 325. King Janaka sends for all three princesses after receiving Sage Vashishtha's direction. Their appearance follows the description of Shri Ram and Mata Sita together on an exalted seat, with King Dashrath rejoicing in their marriage.

faq.q: Does this passage describe Urmila's life during the exile?
faq.a: The passage in Bal Kand, Doha 325, concerns the wedding celebrations and Urmila's appearance in bridal attire. It gives no account of her life during the exile. The fourteen years of exile for Shri Ram, Mata Sita and Lakshman belong to the later narrative in Ayodhya Kand.
